articles.title: Home Assistant brings integration troubleshooting into one view
articles.dek: A new dialog brings failed setup, unavailable entities, repairs and recent log problems together.
body: Home Assistant adds a Health view to each integration connection’s menu, bringing together the clues people need when a device or service stops working. It shows setup status and errors, pending sign-in or reconfiguration, and the entities that are unavailable, with links to the relevant controls.

The same view includes open repairs, recent warnings and errors, and startup setup time. Repairs and log messages currently belong to the whole integration rather than a particular connection, and the dialog labels that scope.

media.alt: Home Assistant integration Health dialog showing connection status and troubleshooting information

articles.title: Let a bedtime story finish its chapter
articles.dek: Music Assistant adds sleep timers based on the end of a chapter or item, rather than only a countdown.
body: Music Assistant adds sleep-timer choices for the end of the current track, podcast episode, audiobook or chapter. The web menu and server work together, so a bedtime listener can stop at a natural break instead of guessing how many minutes remain.

Skipping from Music Assistant moves the timer with the selection. Controls on the speaker have limits: a speaker that already holds the next item can stop when that item is selected, and a skip or seek in the final five seconds can stop other speakers. Fabian Munkes contributes the server and web controls.

articles.title: Home Assistant’s management AI can work through integration setup
articles.dek: Connected assistants gain tools for starting and completing setup forms, with browser sign-in handed back to the user.
body: AI assistants using Home Assistant’s system-management tools gain a way to start setting up an integration or helper and work through its forms. They can read the available fields and choices, submit answers, follow progress or cancel a setup.

Connections that need browser sign-in return a link to Home Assistant’s setup page for the person to finish there. This extends the earlier inspection and reload tools into creating connections and helpers.

articles.title: Home Assistant contains startup failures before they spread
articles.dek: A failed optional connection no longer blocks unrelated Bluetooth, HomeKit and media integrations.
body: Home Assistant keeps an optional integration’s startup failure from stopping other connections that do not need it. A broken Shelly or ESPHome setup could previously prevent Bluetooth adapter discovery, taking roughly sixty Bluetooth integrations and HomeKit Controller down with it.

The correction also separates failures such as Spotify or Plex from Sonos and Cast startup. Home Assistant still waits for the relevant setup attempts to finish and reports their errors; a genuinely required connection must still start successfully.

articles.title: Piper traces voice licenses for commercial projects
articles.dek: New guides trace voice training history and distinguish replacement models from older downloads.
body: Piper adds guides for people choosing a local speech voice for commercial work. Michael Hansen explains how to read each voice’s model card, follow the earlier models it was trained from, and check the licenses through that chain. A separate list identifies voices whose full training chain uses recordings licensed for commercial use.

The guides distinguish replacement voices trained from recordings licensed for commercial use from older downloads based on restricted lessac material. Michael Hansen says the replacement voices are already published; older copies keep their original training history, so the relevant model card is the one supplied with the download. The guides leave open whether a trained model is a derivative work.

pullRequests.title: Document voice licensing and commercial use

articles.title: Foreca gives Home Assistant a longer forecast and its uncertainty
articles.dek: Seven days of hourly forecasts and fourteen daily forecasts join rain and thunderstorm readings.
body: Home Assistant’s Foreca connection expands its hourly forecast from two days to seven and its daily forecast from ten days to fourteen. Both horizons are included in Foreca’s free plan. Daily forecasts also gain cloud cover and the maximum feels-like temperature.

A separate forecast action returns details such as snowfall, sunshine duration and thunderstorm probability, together with ranges for temperature and precipitation that show forecast uncertainty. It uses data already fetched, so calling the action does not make another request.

Current rain intensity, precipitation probability and thunderstorm probability also become sensors for dashboards and automations. Those readings describe current conditions rather than the longer forecast.

articles.title: A lighting library streams to Hue bulbs without a Hue Bridge
articles.dek: The connection targets lights paired with ZHA on Ziggurat, supplying groundwork for applications to adopt.
body: Music Assistant’s Hue Entertainment library adds a way to send rapid lighting updates directly to Hue bulbs paired with Home Assistant’s ZHA, when ZHA runs on Ziggurat. A selected bulb relays each update to the other lights, replacing the Hue Bridge for that stream. Marcel van der Veldt tested real Hue lights at twenty-five updates per second alongside a live ZHA network.

The session saves the lights’ original state and restores it when streaming stops. It gives ordinary ZHA traffic priority and keeps only the newest waiting update. Applications still need to adopt this library connection; the work does not add a bridge-free lighting setting to Music Assistant. This is van der Veldt’s first contribution to the Hue Entertainment repository.

pullRequests.title: Add a Zigbee transport to stream to Hue lights without a Hue bridge

articles.title: Home Assistant automations can repeat while a button is held
articles.dek: A held-button trigger supports continued actions until the button is released.
body: Home Assistant adds a held-button trigger for button event entities. An automation can run when a long press starts, or on release for devices that only report the hold then.

For buttons that report both the start and end of a long press, an optional interval repeats the trigger while the button remains held. Each run includes a repeat count. Repetition stops on another button event or when the entity becomes unavailable, and a thirty-second limit prevents a lost release message from leaving it running indefinitely.

articles.title: Party hosts can require more than one vote to skip
articles.dek: A configurable threshold prevents one guest from deciding every song change.
body: Music Assistant’s Party plugin adds a Votes Required to Skip setting, letting the host require between one and fifty guests before changing songs. The default remains one vote, preserving existing parties’ behavior.
Each guest counts once per song, and votes for a song that has already ended are ignored. Martin Buergi contributes the change in his first contribution to Music Assistant’s server.

articles.title: Home Assistant follows vehicle locations from A Better Routeplanner
articles.dek: Location tracking extends the earlier electric-car readings, and newly added garage vehicles appear automatically.
body: Home Assistant adds a location tracker for each vehicle connected through A Better Routeplanner. It appears when the service first sends a position and follows subsequent telemetry updates, extending the battery and driving readings introduced in October.

Home Assistant also checks the account’s garage hourly for added or shared vehicles, bringing them into the connection without a reload. Garage renames carry over unless the vehicle was renamed in Home Assistant. Vehicles removed from the garage remain until the integration is reloaded.

articles.title: Home Assistant adjusts Sofar battery reserves and inspects individual packs
articles.dek: Cut-off settings become writable, while BTS towers gain pack and cell readings.
body: Home Assistant adds an action for changing Sofar batteries’ discharge limits on and off the grid, their off-grid recovery level and, where supported, their charge cut-off. These settings were previously available as readings. The action writes stored inverter settings, so it skips unchanged values and should not be called frequently.

Sofar BTS towers also gain a device for each battery pack, with capacity, charge-cycle, cell-voltage extremes and temperature readings. Optional sensors expose every reported cell voltage and the pack’s four cell temperatures, helping owners follow cell balance. Pack data refreshes every five minutes.

articles.title: Music Assistant leaves disliked genres out of automatic selections
articles.dek: Genre exclusions cover radio, dynamic playlists and every Autoplay mode, while manual choices stay untouched.
body: Music Assistant applies disliked genres to radio, dynamic playlists and every Autoplay mode. A listener can exclude a whole genre from automatic selections alongside the existing exclusions for individual tracks, albums and artists. Tracks, albums and playlists chosen manually are not filtered.

The check uses the library’s genre information. Tracks with their own genres use those; otherwise the genres of their albums apply. A track that has no matching library entry is not excluded by genre, so this does not promise to filter every recommendation returned by an outside music service.

articles.title: Home Assistant can warn when its storage is wearing out
articles.dek: An optional disk-lifetime sensor makes the host’s wear estimate available to automations.
body: Home Assistant exposes its host disk’s estimated lifetime used as a sensor, allowing an automation to warn about wear and a graph to show its progress. The figure was already visible in system health; the new diagnostic sensor starts disabled.

The estimate is available for eMMC storage and NVMe drives that report their percentage used. Zero represents a new disk and one hundred means the estimated lifetime has been used; eMMC values advance in ten-percentage-point steps. Unsupported disks report an unknown value. MB901 also makes a first contribution to Home Assistant’s website with the accompanying guide.

articles.title: Matter.js fixes missing light controls on Tuya-based bulbs
articles.dek: A compatibility correction handles bulbs from NOUS, Calex and Arlec that leave out part of their device description.
body: Matter.js corrects a pairing failure affecting Tuya-based bulbs including the NOUS Smart Bulb P3 and P4, Calex Smart Light Bulb and Arlec RGB CCT Light. The bulbs could leave pairing unanswered and, after a server restart, appear without a light entity.

The bulbs omit a required part of their device description. Ingo Fischer’s correction lets controllers using Matter.js find the light despite that omission, while logging a warning about the incomplete description.

articles.title: AUX-2 custom firmware builds with stable ESPHome again
articles.dek: Owners taking control can compile the imported configuration, with temporary limits on audio and Zigbee features.
body: AUX-2 owners taking control of their device with ESPHome regain a configuration that builds with the current stable release, 2026.10.2. Recent Zigbee and audio additions had required ESPHome changes absent from that release, preventing the imported configuration from building.

Keith Burzinski separates those additions from the custom configuration. Custom builds retain the USB Zigbee serial proxy and play Sendspin at 16 bits, but omit the newer Zigbee traffic tap. Factory firmware retains its existing features and 24-bit audio. The imported configuration was compiled successfully with ESPHome 2026.10.2.

pullRequests.title: Keep the adopted configuration buildable with the ESPHome release

articles.title: Z-Wave JS starts again when Classic and Long Range share keys
articles.dek: An update had stopped existing networks from starting when the two connection types reused a security key.
body: Z-Wave JS restores startup for existing setups that use the same security key for Z-Wave Classic and Long Range. Since version 15.32.1, the driver rejected that configuration and refused to start.

The correction replaces that startup failure with a warning when a key appears in both groups. Reusing keys within the Classic group itself, or within the Long Range group itself, still causes an error.

pullRequests.title: fix: warn instead of throwing when Classic and LR security keys are shared

articles.title: ESPHome reduces lost data when forwarding serial messages offline
articles.dek: Boards without networking process incoming bytes promptly instead of waiting for their next scheduled update.
body: ESPHome improves serial forwarding on devices configured without Wi-Fi, Ethernet or Thread. Incoming data wakes the device’s main processing loop, avoiding a wait before the bytes are handled.

In two tests on an ESP32-based M5Stack Atom Lite forwarding data between serial ports at 115,200 baud, Bascht74 recorded all 20,000 bytes reaching the output. The previous version forwarded roughly 15,000. Devices with networking keep their existing behavior.

articles.title: Completing a task by voice keeps its notes and due date
articles.dek: Home Assistant changes the task’s status without clearing its other fields.
body: Home Assistant preserves a task’s description and due date when someone marks it done by voice. Previously the completion command replaced the task with only its name, identifier and completed status.
That cleared descriptions and dates in Local To-do and made Todoist tasks lose their notes and deadline. The command now changes only the existing item’s completion status.
